title: Chapter 21
content:
"I heard there was quite a stir earlier today."

Setting his glass down, Chairman Kang broached the morning's incident with casual indifference. Beside him, his wife, Kim Sun-young, used silver tongs to delicately place a choice cut of braised short rib onto his porcelain plate. Across the table, the eyes of the entire family—Seok-joo included—gravitated toward Il-hyun.

"It was nothing, Father," Il-hyun replied smoothly.

Chairman Kang clicked his tongue in mild disapproval. "You nearly caught a bullet between your eyes, and you call that 'nothing'?"

"Well, I'm sitting here in one piece, aren't I?" Il-hyun countered, lifting a piece of tender rib with his chopsticks. He turned a mockingly warm gaze toward Kim Sun-young. "And thanks to that, I even get to enjoy this exquisite meal Stepmother so graciously prepared for us."

Jakyeong caught the subtle provocation immediately. Judging by the venomous way Il-hyun treated Seok-joo, the bad blood between him and the boy's mother was a given. Then again, if anyone actually got along with Kang Il-hyun, that would be the true anomaly.

Sure enough, Sun-young forced a smile so tight the muscles in her cheek visibly twitched.

Rather than reprimand Il-hyun for his insolence, Chairman Kang turned his attention to Jakyeong. "My apologies for subjecting our esteemed guest to such an unsightly spectacle. Please don't take it to heart."

Jakyeong bowed his head with practiced deference. "Not at all, Chairman Kang. I'm completely fine."

"I've been giving it some thought," the patriarch continued, leaning back. "Executive Director Kang's estate seems rather fraught with danger. Why not move into the main house and stay here with us? Seok-joo is here as well."

The sudden offer made the meat Jakyeong had just swallowed feel like a lump of lead in his esophagus. While the gesture was ostensibly generous, he had an objective to retrieve from Il-hyun's private fortress. Besides, living under the old man's roof would be just as suffocating.

Across the table, Seok-joo was practically nodding his head off, frantically gesturing with his eyes for Jakyeong to accept. It was almost comical how the kid acted like they were lifelong bosom buddies after a couple of nights out. A brat will always be a brat.

Jakyeong cut his eyes sideways to gauge Il-hyun's reaction, but the man was merely chewing his food with mechanical indifference, giving nothing away.

"I am deeply grateful for your hospitality, Chairman," Jakyeong answered smoothly, "but I find Director Kang's residence very comfortable. He takes exceptional care of me."

"Is that so?"

The Chairman sounded distinctly skeptical. For a biological father to openly doubt that his son could "take good care" of someone spoke volumes about Il-hyun's reputation.

Beside Jakyeong, the corner of Il-hyun's mouth curved into a faint, satisfied smirk. Why the bastard was pleased was anyone's guess, but he was clearly in high spirits.

As the dinner progressed, casual conversation flowed across the linen tablecloth. On the surface, it seemed remarkably mundane—interspersed with light laughter and polite inquiries—looking for all the world like a normal, harmonious family. Yet beneath the veneer of high-society etiquette, Jakyeong could feel the razor-sharp currents of hostility passing between them.

Who among them hired me to kill Kang Il-hyun?

Before landing in Korea, his primary suspects were Kang Tae-han and Kang Seok-joo—the two brothers with skin in the succession game. Tae-han had the political motive, while Seok-joo was too young and erratic, making his ambitious mother the likely mastermind.

Yet Chairman Kang couldn't be ruled out either. In the underworld, parents putting hits on their own flesh and blood—or children orchestrating patricide—was practically an industry standard. Power had a funny way of making blood ties worth less than dirt. Still, observing them now, the rapport between the Chairman and Il-hyun didn't appear fractured. Though appearances in this family were notoriously deceptive.

And then there was the final, bizarre hypothesis: Did Kang Il-hyun contract the hit on himself?

He still had no answer to that riddle. Wang Han had reached out that morning to report that Dmitri had flown to Russia for an impromptu vacation and wouldn't return for several days. Of all the damn times to go off the grid.

"Care for a drink, young man?"

Chairman Kang's voice broke his train of thought, gesturing toward the liquor decanter.

Jakyeong managed an awkward, bashful smile. "I... I don't hold my liquor very well, Chairman..."

"Hahaha! Well, you certainly didn't take after your father in that regard," the old man chuckled.

"My apologies, sir."

"Nonsense, have a glass anyway. A young man ought to learn how to drink from his elders. Accept it as if it were poured by your own father."

Unable to refuse, Jakyeong held his crystal tumbler with both hands in deep respect. The pale amber liquor had a rich, intoxicating aroma and went down surprisingly smooth. Il-hyun cast a brief glance his way, but offered no objection.

After several rounds of accepting toasts from the patriarch, the alcohol began to catch up with him.

Jakyeong had never been a heavy drinker—two or three cans of beer were usually his limit. He fought to maintain his composure, but before long, the voices around the table morphed into a dull, echoing hum. His eyelids grew impossibly heavy, a wave of exhaustion washing over him.

Noticing his state, Il-hyun quietly excused himself from the table for a moment and returned with a tall glass of ice water, setting it down beside Jakyeong.

Jakyeong forced his eyes open, willing his pupils to focus so as not to betray his drunkenness, only for Il-hyun to softly ask if he was holding up. The unexpected consideration caught him off guard, evoking a strange flutter of gratitude. Il-hyun's smile was surprisingly tender, and his dark eyes—perhaps a trick of the alcohol—held a fleeting warmth.

Jakyeong gave a docile nod and stared forward, the heat in his flushed cheeks burning hotter by the second.

His head kept lolling to the side.

No matter how hard Jakyeong tried to snap himself awake, his limbs refused to obey. Getting plastered off a few glasses of high-end liquor was humiliating, but a hazy part of his mind simply wanted to pass out and sleep like the dead. Ever since setting foot in Korea, he hadn't experienced a single night of uninterrupted rest.

His vision blurred into a smear of city lights before his consciousness drifted entirely away.

When he finally blinked his eyes open, something felt remarkably off about the texture pressing against his cheek. Lifting his heavy head, he found Kang Il-hyun’s sharp profile mere inches from his nose.

With a jolt of pure adrenaline, Jakyeong realized he had been fast asleep, dead to the world, resting his head directly on Kang Il-hyun’s shoulder.

He recoiled in sheer horror, scrambling backward against the car door.

Il-hyun turned his head, a quiet amusement playing on his lips. "Did you sleep well?"

"I... I am so sorry," Jakyeong stammered, his face burning. "I didn't realize I fell asleep on your shoulder..."

"Don't worry about it. My shoulders are broad enough to handle a little extra weight."

"..."

Why the hell is he flexing his physique out of nowhere?

Jakyeong discreetly wiped the corner of his mouth to ensure he hadn't drooled. Sleeping soundly on the shoulder of the very man he was contracted to assassinate—unbelievable. Stellar professional conduct.

Cursing himself internally, he glanced out the window, his eyes widening in confusion.

The luxury sedan was parked in an unfamiliar underground garage. Looking around, the driver and passenger seats up front were completely empty. A realization struck him: Il-hyun had been sitting here in the quiet, letting him sleep on his shoulder for quite some time.

"Where... are we?"

"My place."

"Your house, Director Kang?"

"We're staying here tonight," Il-hyun said, unbuckling his seatbelt. "I'm too exhausted to make the drive all the way out to the outskirts."

Il-hyun pushed his door open and stepped out, with Jakyeong trailing close behind. The subterranean garage was sprawling, packed with multi-hundred-thousand-dollar imported supercars.

Approaching the private residential entrance, Il-hyun tapped an encrypted keycard against the scanner, and the heavy glass doors glided open. Uniformed security personnel stationed throughout the lobby bowed in unison.

Passing through the grand foyer, the building opened up into a self-contained luxury complex—boasting fine dining restaurants and designer boutiques akin to a high-end department store.

They rode an escalator to the upper concourse, which featured private screening rooms, an indoor infinity pool, event lounges, guest suites, and a full-scale fitness center. Boarding a private elevator in the central atrium, Il-hyun swiped his card, and the panel automatically illuminated the 13th floor.

When the doors chimed open, Jakyeong noted that the entire floor was divided into only two sprawling penthouse units.

Il-hyun turned, asking which side he preferred to sleep in.

Jakyeong’s eyes widened. He owns both penthouses on this floor?

When Jakyeong hesitated, Il-hyun made the call, heading toward the right-hand unit with the promise that the skyline view was superior.

The moment the heavy double doors clicked open, motion sensors activated, bathing the expansive penthouse in warm, ambient light.

Jakyeong froze at the threshold.

The interior was vibrant, cozy, and adorned with delicate, charming decor—a complete, jarring antithesis to the cold, fortified minimalism of Il-hyun's country mansion.

"Your tastes certainly span the extreme ends of the spectrum," Jakyeong remarked before he could filter his thoughts.

Il-hyun let out a dry, self-deprecating chuckle. "This is my sister's handiwork. I went away on an overseas business trip and returned to find she had turned my penthouse into this."

Ah. That makes infinitely more sense. It looked entirely out of character for him. Still, knowing Il-hyun's tyrannical temper, the fact that he hadn't gutted the place and remodeled it from scratch was surprising.

Browsing the living room, Jakyeong’s eyes lit up as he examined the whimsical trinkets lining the shelves. He actually shared a private fondness for collecting small, unique ornaments—a quirky habit Wang Han had never understood.

His fingers brushed against a small, handcrafted porcelain elephant, and he gently picked it up. Elephants had always been his favorite animals: massive, reliable, intelligent, and fiercely loyal to their herd.

"Your sister and I seem to share very similar tastes," Jakyeong smiled, looking over his shoulder.

Il-hyun was staring back at him, his face completely devoid of expression.

"Do you like her?"

"Pardon?"

"You seemed remarkably taken with Kang Yu-jung earlier. I was wondering if a woman like her is your type."

Jakyeong blinked, caught off guard. Well, what red-blooded man wouldn't find a woman like that attractive? She was gorgeous, had a wonderfully candid personality, and was a brilliant surgeon to boot—meaning if he ever caught a stray bullet on the job, she could patch him up in no time.

The thought brought an involuntary, amused quirk to the corner of his lips.

Il-hyun’s left eyebrow arched into a sharp, skeptical angle. "You're smiling?"

"Wh-Who's smiling...?"

"And stuttering."

Jakyeong stared at him, flabbergasted. Is he seriously warning me to keep my hands off his sister?

Their gazes locked, Il-hyun’s expression remaining chillingly cold.

"Keep dreaming," Il-hyun drawled flatly. "You're nowhere near her type."

A sudden, sharp realization flickered in Jakyeong’s mind.

Could Kang Il-hyun genuinely be interested in me?

The incident in the basement vault, the bizarre physical reaction during the sniper tackle... those were hardly things a straight syndicate boss did to another man by accident.

If that was the case, why not exploit it? If he played into the attraction, he could manipulate Il-hyun into lowering his guard completely. But what if it was a trap? Emotions in this business were easily fabricated.

Should I test the waters?

"Then what about you, Director Kang?" Jakyeong asked, his voice dropping into a subtle, suggestive lilt.

A microscopic twitch rippled beneath Il-hyun's eye.

"What is your type?"

Whatever Il-hyun read in Jakyeong's expression, his deadpan mask melted into a low, amused smirk.

"Look at you, acting cute."

Il-hyun closed the distance between them with slow, measured strides.

This time, Jakyeong did not take a step back. Standing right before him was a five-million-dollar bounty. That wasn't pocket change—it was his ticket out of the underworld forever.

Il-hyun’s hand came to rest on Jakyeong’s shoulder, his fingers sliding with agonizing slowness up the side of his neck. With every brush of skin against skin, the tension in Jakyeong’s throat tightened to a suffocating coil.

Reaching his cheek, Il-hyun’s fingertips tapped lightly against the cheekbone—like keys on a piano—before his entire palm cupped Jakyeong's face. The heat radiating from his hand was searing.

"Do you really want to know?" Il-hyun murmured softly.

Jakyeong held his tongue, his chest rising and falling in shallow breaths.

"Tell me, Yi-an. Are you truly that curious?"

Jakyeong parted his tightly clamped lips.

Fuck it. Five million dollars. Five million dollars.

The man standing in front of him wasn't a lethal mob boss—he was a five-million-dollar asset waiting to be cashed in.

"Yes," Jakyeong whispered, holding his gaze. "Show me."

The corner of Il-hyun's mouth curved into a wicked, triumphant crescent. The hand cradling Jakyeong's cheek slid smoothly around to the nape of his neck, pulling him forward as Il-hyun’s lips descended slowly toward his mouth.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Korean Drinking Etiquette (술은 어른한테 배워야 한다): In Korean culture, receiving a drink from an elder or higher-status figure requires holding the glass with both hands and turning slightly away from them when sipping as a sign of respect. Chairman Kang treating Jakyeong like a surrogate son highlights how deeply entrenched the patriarchal syndicate ties are between the families.

  • Seoul Super-Luxury High-Rises (초고화 주상복합): Complexes like Tower Palace, Nine One Hannam, or Signiel Residences in Seoul feature ultra-exclusive private residential amenities—including Michelin-starred dining, luxury retail boutiques, private concierges, and multi-car underground private garages where multi-million-dollar sports cars are commonplace.
